claims.assertion: Ley 11/2023 Title I transposes the EAA for listed products and consumer services.
claims.review_note: Current consolidated BOE opened on 2026-09-24. EAA context; not the WAD. Link reachable at BOE.

claims.assertion: The existing Yes means a dedicated public EAA accessibility-statement page is required on a company's website.
claims.review_note: Existing ✔️ Yes preserved with explicit EAA-specific source-needed qualification. In user-supplied 'Questions about reporting for the EAA (8).eml', the 24 September 2026 outgoing message asks UTAC whether a company website must publish a public accessibility statement; no response to that question appears. The existing row refers to arts. 7–9, which concern product-side requirements rather than proof of a dedicated service page. Before-merge manual research task; do not infer No. Update 2026-09-25: UTAC replied to the follow-up but deferred substantive answers, hoping to answer these questions in 2027. Statement question remains unresolved; preserve existing Yes and source-needed qualification.

claims.assertion: Providers include information assessing how the service meets accessibility requirements in their general terms or equivalent document.
claims.review_note: Separate isolated Spanish-to-English language review on 2026-09-24: correction applied to retain 'assessing how' and Art. 3; final English wording rechecked against literal rendering. Original excerpt 'incluirán, en las condiciones generales o documento equivalente, la información que evalúe de qué manera el servicio cumple...' Literal: include in general terms or equivalent information assessing how the service meets requirements. Initial shortened wording needed correction; final claim preserves assessment of how.

claims.assertion: The Art. 13 information is publicly available in written and oral form and accessible to persons with disabilities.
claims.review_note: This is a public availability obligation; it does not by itself prove a separate statement page.

claims.assertion: The public may request information separately from the required publicly available Art. 13 information.
claims.review_note: Do not conflate public availability with a separate public-on-request duty.

claims.assertion: Providers furnish all information necessary to demonstrate service conformity on a reasoned competent-authority request.
claims.review_note: Isolated language review corrected the shortened wording to retain 'all information necessary' and reasoned request. Original excerpt 'Sobre la base de una solicitud motivada ... toda la información necesaria...' Literal: on a reasoned request, all necessary information. Final claim supported after correction.

claims.assertion: Autonomous communities and Ceuta/Melilla determine surveillance authorities within their competences; other authorities' powers under supplementary regulations remain possible.
claims.review_note: Statutory authority class rather than an exhaustive current named roster. Isolated Spanish review supported wording with 'determine' and powers caveat. Existing UTAC-only display misleadingly suggested it was sole surveillance body. Individual regional designations were not verified within this pass. Language agent final wording check: 'retain powers' was rejected; use 'may have powers' to preserve conditional pudiera tener. Table omits supplementary-powers detail for brevity.
claims.scope: Products, E-commerce, Banking, Electronic communications, Transport, Audiovisual access, E-books

claims.assertion: UTAC coordinates and supports surveillance authorities and serves as an information contact for citizens and economic operators.
claims.review_note: UTAC government link opened to correct agency. It is not the universal designated regional supervisor. Isolated agent found coordination/support not established by the supplied art. 3(g),(h) excerpts alone; art. 3(a) and official UTAC page explicitly supply that role.

claims.assertion: UTAC acts as the surveillance authority in areas where none has been designated.
claims.review_note: Isolated language review supported this precise conditional wording. Does not prove that a particular region/sector is currently undesignated. Language agent final verdict Supported: 'acts as surveillance authority where none has been designated.'

claims.assertion: Individual designated authorities are named and verified for each region and product/service sector.
claims.review_note: No verified complete current public roster found in bounded research. Keep statutory class and coordination body; do not claim named regional coverage.

claims.assertion: A named authority is established for accessibility of 112 emergency-call answering.
claims.review_note: The specific answering-centre oversight body and reporting route were not verified; separate from electronic-communications providers.

claims.assertion: The public can send Ley 11/2023 accessibility noncompliance reports or complaints to UTAC by email.
claims.review_note: Published UTAC page opened and identified the precise EAA purpose; email has no login prerequisite. UTAC coordinates and may direct matters within its remit; this is not proof it is the final local deciding authority. Language agent final verdict Supported for 'Public complaints and reports' and instruction to describe the Ley 11/2023 case.
